task-intent.statement: Make the lane green on its own full Linux suite without weakening what the approved change proved.

expected-behavior.statement: A change confined to one branch of one advisory string, approved by an independent reviewer on the issue's own anchor test class, leaves the rest of the suite green.

observed-behavior.statement: Three tests in a DIFFERENT class failed, because that class deliberately pins the whole advisory string byte-for-byte to detect exactly this kind of silent drift. The targeted selector the reviewer ran could not see them.

impact-cost.statement: An approved, merge-ready lane could not merge, and a whole repair wave was needed to close four failures that a single full-suite run at review time would have surfaced.

workaround.statement: When a change edits a string rendered through a shared helper, take the acceptance evidence from every test that pins that helper's output rather than from the issue's anchor class alone; the cheapest reliable form is one cache-clean full-suite run before the review verdict.

diagnosis.statement: The three expectations were stale, not the shipped wording: all three scenarios leave the active gate PENDING, and the engine refuses `advance` on a pending gate, so the pre-change wording named a command the engine rejects -- which is the defect the issue set out to fix.
Realign each call site to the expectation helper matching the gate status its own scenario produces, preserving the class's whole-string equality property; delete no test.

A stale .pyc carrying the pre-relocation path `constellation-skills-wt/` had already fabricated a phantom failure in this wave, so every suite count here was taken after clearing __pycache__; the four failures reproduced exactly, confirming they were real.
